items.title: Chicago City Council aldermen push for ShotSpotter reinstatement and millionaire tax after voter approval
items.summary: A coalition of aldermen in the City Council Budget Accountability Coalition announced plans to call for votes on two advisory measures that voters supported last week: restoring the ShotSpotter gunshot detection system, which the mayor ended in September 2024, and a millionaire’s tax that the mayor backs. The group will seek votes at next week’s council meeting as Mayor Brandon Johnson’s proposed 2027 budget still lacks the 26 votes needed for passage before the Dec. 31 deadline.

items.title: Merchants sue over federal rules exempting banks from Illinois swipe‑fee ban
items.summary: Retailers filed lawsuits claiming federal regulators exceeded their authority by allowing national banks and credit unions to bypass Illinois’ law that bans credit and debit card swipe fees on sales taxes and tips. The suits, reported by Bloomberg Law, seek to block the exemptions and protect the state’s effort to eliminate these fees.

items.summary: Jessica Biggs won the high‑profile Chicago School Board president race, defeating former CTU organizer Hilario Dominguez and attorney Victor Henderson. Biggs was backed by the union representing Chicago Public School support staff and the Common Ground Collective super PAC. Her victory makes her the first elected president of the CPS board.

items.title: Democratic lawmakers organize opposition to Speaker Emanuel "Chris" Welch in Illinois House
items.summary: A group of Democratic state representatives is quietly trying to organize opposition to Speaker Emanuel "Chris" Welch ahead of a speaker vote expected in January. Lawmakers cite Welch's handling of a sexual harassment complaint involving former Rep. Harry Benton, a 60‑vote rule for measures, and broader frustrations with House operations. The effort reflects growing tension in Springfield as legislators prepare for the upcoming veto session.

items.title: Gov. JB Pritzker wins third term and unveils “Fighting for Illinois” agenda
items.summary: Incumbent Governor JB Pritzker defeated Republican Darren Bailey on Nov. 3, 2026 to win a third term. After his victory speech at Chicago’s Navy Pier, he introduced the “Fighting for Illinois: The Day One Agenda,” a set of nearly 200 policy proposals aimed at addressing everyday challenges. The agenda was presented as part of his plan to fight for Illinois at the state and federal levels.

items.title: City Hall hosts mobile food car licensing ordinance rally
items.summary: At 9 a.m. on Nov. 4, 2026, city officials gathered at City Hall for a rally on a new mobile food car licensing ordinance. The event, featuring remarks by Brandon, aimed to discuss the proposed licensing rules for mobile food vendors and coincided with an online Native American Heritage Month cultural reception.

items.title: The Nov. 4 Skyline is out
items.summary: The Nov. 4, 2026 edition of Skyline is out, a day after the midterm election. Editor Tom O'Gorman says more election results are still coming in and the paper will keep reporting on them. The full issue is available from Inside Publications.

items.title: Illinois' blue wave
items.summary: Illinois voters turned out yesterday in an election marked by long lines, sporadic polling-place problems and historic results. Yesterday's results will shape Illinois' political leadership and representation in Washington, while offering a glimpse of how Chicago voters may feel about Mayor Brandon Johnson and the Chicago Teachers Union. (more on that below) Gov.

items.title: State Rep. La Shawn Ford Wins Race To Succeed Danny Davis In 7th Congressional District
items.summary: Ford will be the district's first new leader in 30 years, replacing the retiring U.S. Rep. Danny Davis.

items.title: What to expect after the midterm results
items.summary: POLITICO Forecast laid out what to watch once Tuesday's midterm results came in, including a likely return to divided government in Washington if Democrats win the House. It expects more legislative gridlock, budget standoffs, and a wave of congressional investigations, along with the immediate start of the 2028 presidential contest in both parties.

items.title: Voting underway at Loop Supersite
items.summary: Darius Johnson reports live from the Loop Supersite. Lines are under 30 minutes, and Darius said voting takes around 10 minutes once inside.

items.title: Black Harvest Film Festival Celebrates 32nd Year With Lineup For Us, By Us'
items.summary: The festival showcasing films created by Black artists returns to the School of the Art Institute of Chicago’s Gene Siskel Film Center Friday through Nov. 15 with 10 shorts as well as feature-length films.

items.title: Chicago school board president race pits CTU‑backed Hilario Dominguez against SEIU‑endorsed Jessica Biggs
items.summary: The contest for Chicago school board president has CTU‑backed Hilario Dominguez framing the fight as a stand against outside influence, while billionaire Michael Sacks backs his opponent Jessica Biggs, who is supported by two SEIU groups. The race is seen as an early test of the city’s progressive coalition and could signal trends for the February mayoral election. Both CTU and SEIU are prominent progressive labor groups in Chicago.

items.title: Illinois Democrats raise record $141.85 million through ActBlue in 2026 midterms
items.summary: ActBlue reported that Illinois Democrats collected $141.85 million in the 2026 midterm cycle, a 15.5 percent increase over 2022, with 1.04 million donors contributing 6.7 percent more than four years ago. ActBlue CEO Regina Wallace‑Jones highlighted the surge during a Chicago stop on her cross‑country tour, handing out coffee and donuts to voters. The fundraising boost positions Illinois as a strong blue pillar in the Midwest.

items.title: Election storylines to watch
items.summary: Illinois voters head to the polls today to decide who will lead the state, represent them in Washington and oversee Chicago's public schools. Beyond the marquee races for governor and U. Senate, the results could reshape political power in our area for years to come.

items.title: Polls open for Illinois 2026 midterm election
items.summary: As Darious Johnson reports, voters are already lined up outside the Loop supersite.

items.title: Woman issues warning after Uber driver cancels ride, drives wrong way mid-trip
items.summary: Her Uber app shows a location on Hubbard as the drop-off address, but she says they were able to finally get out of the car on Randolph Street near the Kennedy Expressway.

items.title: Neon Trees, Michael James Scott, Thelma Houston To Headline Magnificent Mile Lights Parade
items.summary: The 35th annual festival and parade returns Saturday, Nov. 21 with live performances, floats, a fireworks spectacular and one million lights along Michigan Avenue.

items.title: Chef John Manion Is Bringing A New Kind Of Steakhouse To The West Loop With Palomino
items.summary: Opening in the former Proxi on Randolph Street, Palomino will focus on live-fire cooking and the flavors and techniques of the American West and South.

items.title: 5 Must-See Theater Shows To Check Out In November
items.summary: Brand-new shows and revivals of decades-old classics share the spotlight on Chicago stages this month.

items.title: Our Votes Count March set for downtown Chicago on Saturday, Nov. 7
items.summary: Indivisible Chicago is organizing an "Our Votes Count" march in downtown Chicago on Saturday, Nov. 7, at noon, and Indivisible Greater West Loop is asking members to sign up. The group also points voters to its Voter Resource Hub for information on races, advisory questions, polling places, and hours ahead of Election Day on Tuesday, Nov. 3.

items.title: Volunteer shift at the Food Depository Nov. 13 and a Paint, Sip, Give fundraiser Nov. 18
items.summary: Indivisible Greater West Loop is recruiting volunteers for a Friday, Nov. 13 shift at the Greater Chicago Food Depository, 12:45 to 3:30 p.m., repackaging bulk donations into smaller portions for local families. On Wednesday, Nov. 18, from 6 to 8:30 p.m., the group hosts a Paint, Sip, Give holiday fundraiser with Chicago Sip & Paint benefiting the Chicago Food Sovereignty Coalition. The group also staffs a table at the West Loop Farmers Market on Saturdays, 8 to 11:30 a.m.

items.title: Open Books nonprofit bookstore soon to close West Loop Chicago location
items.summary: Open Books​ is closing its location in Chicago's West Loop, citing a decline in foot traffic and the rising cost of running a store in that community.

items.title: Open Books to close store in Chicago's West Loop
items.summary: Open Books is closing its location in Chicago’s West Loop, citing a decline in foot traffic and the rising cost of running a store in that community.

items.title: Gov. JB Pritzker urges Chicago churchgoers to vote, highlights new student voter registration law
items.summary: On Nov. 1, Gov. JB Pritzker spoke at the Apostolic Church of God in Chicago, invoking Rev. Jesse Jackson’s legacy and urging congregants to turn out for Democrats. He promoted Illinois’ new law that requires high school students to be registered to vote and the state mandate that Black history be taught in public schools. Pritzker also praised Senate nominee Juliana Stratton and warned that a vote for Republican Mike Rogers would aid Donald Trump.

items.title: Cook County Commissioner Sean Morrison publicly opposes GOP nominee Liz Gorman in board race
items.summary: Republican Cook County Commissioner Sean Morrison posted on Facebook that Liz Gorman should never be allowed to hold public office, reflecting a long‑running rivalry. His comment came as the county board races heat up, with Gorman facing Democrat Elyse Hoffenberg for the Lyons Township Clerk seat. Cook County Democrats are hoping to sweep the board races while Republicans aim to retain at least one seat.

items.title: Chicago's 2026 Christmas Tree Is A Nearly 50-Foot Spruce From Kane County
items.summary: The tree will be cut and transported to Chicago Monday from Campton Hills. It'll light up Millennium Park Nov. 20-Jan. 10.

items.title: The dark side of daylight saving
items.summary: Chicagoans turned back their clocks yesterday, gaining an extra hour of sleep but losing an hour of evening daylight. Could this be the last time? President Trump and House lawmakers want to make daylight saving time permanent, but the change would come with a significant trade-off for Chicago: Winter sunrises wouldn't arrive until after 8am.

items.title: Why the world is watching Tuesday's U.S. midterm elections
items.summary: POLITICO Forecast lays out eight reasons the Nov. 3 midterms matter beyond U.S. borders, including control of congressional committees and spending, the future of the Iran war and Ukraine aid, AI regulation, and tariff policy. The newsletter notes 36 governors' races are also on the ballot and could shape the rollout of data centers. It also previews the start of the 2028 presidential race once results are in.

items.title: The Escape Game opens a new Fulton Market location
items.summary: The Escape Game opened its new Fulton Market location on Oct. 23 and has joined the West Central Association. The venue offers 60-minute team adventures with movie-quality sets, multiple rooms, and unlimited hints, aimed at friends, families, and corporate groups of a wide range of ages and skill levels.

items.title: BrightPath West Loop child care center opens at 310 S. Racine
items.summary: BrightPath West Loop, an early learning and child care center at 310 S. Racine Ave., celebrated its ribbon cutting with the West Central Association. The center serves children from six weeks to five years old and is offering tours to families.

items.title: Illinois Medical District opens new park and COVID-19 memorial
items.summary: The Illinois Medical District cut the ribbon on a new park and COVID-19 memorial near Ogden Avenue, Damen Avenue, and Polk Street. The space features three stainless-steel dandelion sculptures honoring frontline and essential workers and remembering those lost to COVID-19, and is designed as a place to gather and reflect.

items.title: A couple of striking Halloween displays | What Caught My Eye
items.summary: Suzanne Le Mignot shows us a terrifying Halloween spectacle put together by 24-year-old Sam Darr, while Shane Hinton shows us a light-centric Halloween display in the West Loop that features a skeleton throwing up.

items.title: Open Books Closing In West Loop, Selling Inventory At Half Off
items.summary: The nonprofit's last remaining retail location in Chicago will be in Pilsen after the Lake Street store closes Nov. 8.

items.title: Should Chicago Have Milwaukee-Style Public Festival Grounds?
items.summary: Festivals like Lollapalooza and Riot Fest leave sections of public parks closed for weeks, frustrating some residents. A ballot question is meant to be a conversation starter about alternatives, one alderman said.

items.title: City budget hearings focus on $520 million TIF sweep and proposed 15‑cent “Nickel and Dime” tax
items.summary: Alderman Bill Conway attended recent Chicago City Council budget hearings where the Mayor’s 2027 budget proposal was examined. Key issues include a $520 million TIF surplus that the Mayor plans to sweep, inconsistencies in applying the sweep formula, and a proposed 15‑cent “Nickel and Dime” package tax that would affect grocery and prescription deliveries. The hearings also addressed a stalled gunshot‑detection procurement and the need for more resources for streets and sanitation amid increasing severe weather.

items.title: City budget hearings focus on TIF sweep, proposed taxes, and public safety technology
items.summary: Alderman Conway attended City Council budget hearings on the Mayor's 2027 budget, highlighting a $520 million TIF sweep that appears inconsistently applied, a proposed 15‑cent “Nickel and Dime” tax that could affect grocery and prescription deliveries, unresolved procurement of gunshot detection technology, and the need for more resources for streets and sanitation amid severe weather. He pledged to keep scrutinizing the proposals as hearings continue.

items.title: CTA Bus Vision Project seeks rider input; community meeting Nov 17 at CTA headquarters
items.summary: The Chicago Transit Authority is gathering feedback for its Bus Vision Project and will hold a community engagement meeting in the 34th Ward on November 17 from 5 p.m. to 7 p.m. at the CTA headquarters, 567 W Lake. Residents can also take an online survey or attend other events to shape future bus service improvements.

items.title: Mayor's Proposed 2027 Budget Faces Scrutiny in City Council Hearings
items.summary: During City Council budget hearings, the 34th Ward representative examined the Mayor’s 2027 budget, highlighting concerns over $40 billion in unfunded pension liabilities and $31 billion in debt. The representative questioned the $520 million TIF sweep, the proposed 15‑cent "Nickel and Dime" tax, and the unresolved procurement of gun‑shot detection technology. He emphasized the need for responsible spending, affordable housing, and job growth to address the city’s structural deficit.

items.title: CTA Bus Vision Project Seeks 34th Ward Input at November 17 Meeting
items.summary: CTA is gathering feedback from riders and non‑riders to improve bus service under its Bus Vision Project. Residents of the 34th Ward can attend a community engagement meeting on November 17 from 5‑7 pm at CTA headquarters, 567 W. Lake. Participants can also take a survey or learn more on the project site.

items.title: City Council Budget Hearings Focus on 2027 Budget and Fiscal Challenges
items.summary: Council member spent week in budget hearings, examining Mayor’s proposed 2027 budget. Key issues include $40B in unfunded pension liabilities, $31B in debt, and a $520M TIF sweep that may not be applied consistently. The hearings also addressed a proposed 15‑cent “Nickel and Dime” tax, gunshot detection technology procurement, and the need for more affordable housing and jobs.

items.title: CTA Bus Vision Project Seeks Rider Feedback in 34th Ward
items.summary: CTA is gathering input from riders and non‑riders to improve bus service. A community engagement meeting will be held on November 17 from 5‑7pm at CTA headquarters, 567 W. Lake. Residents can also take a survey or learn more on the project site.

items.title: Chicago Youth Climate Action Fund Offers Grants to 15‑24‑Year‑Olds
items.summary: The city invites young people to apply for $1,000–$5,000 grants to develop environmental projects. Eligible projects include environmental justice advocacy, community gardens, tree planting, recycling, composting, food‑waste reduction, clean‑energy education, sustainable transportation, and other climate solutions. Applications are open through November 6, 2026.

items.title: Alderman highlights concerns in 2027 City budget hearings
items.summary: During a week of City Council budget hearings, the 34th Ward Alderman examined the Mayor's proposed 2027 budget, noting roughly $40 billion in unfunded pension liabilities and $31 billion in debt. He raised questions about the $520 million TIF sweep that appears inconsistently applied, warned that the proposed 15‑cent “Nickel and Dime” tax could burden families, and called for transparency on the stalled gunshot detection procurement. The hearings continue next week as officials seek ways to fund affordable housing and essential services.

items.title: CTA Bus Vision Project holds community meeting in the 34th Ward
items.summary: The Chicago Transit Authority is inviting riders and non‑riders to share feedback on bus service as part of its Bus Vision Project. A community engagement meeting is scheduled for November 17 from 5 p.m. to 7 p.m. at CTA headquarters, 567 W. Lake, where participants can discuss improvements for routes that serve the West Loop, Fulton Market and surrounding neighborhoods.

items.title: Chicago Youth Climate Action Fund opens applications for $1,000‑$5,000 grants
items.summary: The City of Chicago is accepting applications from young people ages 15 to 24 for the Youth Climate Action Fund, offering grants between $1,000 and $5,000 to support projects such as community gardens, tree planting, recycling, clean‑energy education and sustainable transportation. Applications remain open through November 6, 2026, providing an opportunity for local youth to lead climate solutions in the 34th Ward and beyond.

items.title: Halloween at the Glessner House in Chicago's South Loop
items.summary: Go inside the Glessner House in Chicago's South Loop for some history and hauntings with Jackie Kosktek.

items.title: 5 Candidates File To Run In 27th Ward, Challenging Burnett Family's Decades-Long Hold On Seat
items.summary: Ald. Walter Redmond Burnett, appointed last year after his father retired following 30 years in office, faces four challengers as he seeks his first election victory.

items.title: Chicago Avenue Bridge Reopening Delayed To Next Spring As Alderman Fumes
items.summary: Concurrent bridge closures Downtown and on the North Side have disrupted daily life for commuters. Ald. Brendan Reilly called the project planning a "massive bureaucratic failure."

items.title: 42nd Ward Alderman Brendan Reilly Faces One Challenger In 2027 Election
items.summary: It could be the first time Reilly has faced a challenger on the ballot since being elected in 2007.

items.title: 2027 mayoral candidate George Cardenas releases AI‑generated database of 1.5 million Chicago voters
items.summary: Board of Review commissioner George Cardenas has launched a website that publicly displays the home addresses, birth years and voting histories of more than 1.5 million Chicago residents. The data was compiled using AI tools by the Illinois Answers Project’s Andrew Adams and Alex Nitkin, raising concerns about privacy and voter information security ahead of the 2027 mayoral race.

items.title: Independent candidate Chris Getty challenges Patty Garcia in Illinois’s 4th Congressional District
items.summary: Chris Getty, a Democrat‑turned‑independent, is challenging Patty Garcia for the Democratic nomination in Illinois’s 4th Congressional District. The Independent PAC has spent $250,000 on Getty’s campaign and he has raised more than $400,000, while Garcia’s campaign has raised $527,000 and is backed by House Minority Leader Hakeem Jeffries and Gov. JB Pritzker. Getty hopes to appeal to independents and Hispanic voters, and a recent meet‑and‑greet at Brookfield’s Irish Times Pub drew nearly 300 attendees.

items.title: Gov. JB Pritzker and other Illinois Democrats to attend get‑out‑the‑vote rally
items.summary: Gov. JB Pritzker, Cook County Board President Toni Preckwinkle, Senate candidate Juliana Stratton and Congressman Danny Davis will attend a get‑out‑the‑vote rally on Saturday, aiming to boost turnout ahead of the midterm elections. The rally is part of a broader effort by Illinois Democrats to mobilize voters across the state.

items.title: Independent Chris Getty challenges Patty Garcia in Illinois 4th Congressional District race
items.summary: Chris Getty, a Democrat‑turned‑independent backed by the Independent PAC, is contesting Patty Garcia for the Democratic nomination in the 4th Congressional District, a majority‑Hispanic area that includes parts of Chicago and its western suburbs. Getty has received $250,000 from the Independent PAC and has raised more than $400,000 himself, while Garcia’s campaign has raised $527,000 and is supported by House Minority Leader Hakeem Jeffries and Gov. JB Pritzker. The race tests voter backlash over Rep. Chuy García’s decision to step aside and highlights the growing influence of independent candidates in Illinois politics.

items.title: Board of Review commissioner George Cardenas releases AI‑generated database of 1.5 million Chicago voters
items.summary: George Cardenas, a candidate for mayor and current Cook County Board of Review commissioner, launched a website that publicly lists the home addresses, birth years and voting histories of more than 1.5 million Chicago residents. The data was compiled using artificial‑intelligence tools developed by the Illinois Answers Project, raising concerns about privacy and the potential misuse of voter information. The site has drawn criticism from privacy advocates and prompted calls for regulatory scrutiny.

items.title: Gov. JB Pritzker and local leaders headline get‑out‑the‑vote rally ahead of midterm elections
items.summary: Governor JB Pritzker, Cook County Board President Toni Preckwinkle, Senate candidate Juliana Stratton and Congressman Danny Davis are scheduled to appear at a rally on Saturday to encourage voter turnout for the upcoming midterm elections. The event is part of a statewide effort to mobilize Democratic voters and features speeches on the importance of protecting health care, immigration reforms and other key issues. Organizers expect a large turnout from neighborhoods across Chicago, including the Near West Side and South Loop.

items.title: Election Day security
items.summary: Stock: Getty Images City election officials are coordinating with local, state and federal law enforcement agencies to protect voters from potential disruptions at the polls on Election Day. The preparations come amid heightened concerns about federal immigration enforcement near polling places and the possibility of voter intimidation. The Chicago Board of Election Commissioners tells Axios it has coordinated.

items.title: Consumer groups hand deliver 10k comments opposing $144M Peoples Gas rate hike
items.summary: Environmental and consumer advocates marched through downtown Chicago on Thursday to deliver more than 10,000 petitions urging regulators to reject Peoples Gas' latest rate case.

items.title: Advocates protest proposed $144 million rate hike for Peoples Gas

items.title: 2026 midterms become the most expensive U.S. election on record
items.summary: Tracking service AdImpact reports that political ad spending across the 2025-2026 midterm cycle has passed $11.2 billion, more than the 2024 presidential cycle. About $801 million in TV ads in top races has focused on affordability alone, with Democrats spending $401 million and Republicans $311 million on the issue. The national average gas price stands at $4.22 a gallon ahead of Election Day on Nov. 3.

items.title: What time does trick-or-treating start in Chicago this Saturday?
items.summary: Halloween falls on Saturday, Oct. 31, and unlike many suburbs, Chicago does not set official trick-or-treating hours, so neighborhoods decide for themselves. Suburbs are running Halloween hours between noon and 8pm, with Schaumburg and Arlington Heights starting at 3pm. In an Axios reader poll, 57% favored sticking with the traditional 4pm start. Households not ready for visitors are advised to turn off the porch light.

items.title: Halloween weekend picks: parades, dog costumes and Rocky Horror
items.summary: The free Streeterville Dog Halloween Party runs Saturday 9-11am at the MCA, and the 30th annual Haunted Halsted Halloween Parade steps off Saturday at 7pm on Halsted between Aldine and Addison, with $4,000 in costume prizes. The Chicago Theatre screens a 4K restoration of The Rocky Horror Picture Show with a live shadow cast Saturday at 7:30pm ($84). Pilsen's Dia de los Muertos Window Walk along 18th Street continues through Nov. 2.

items.title: Green, Pink Line Train Service Restored Downtown After Shutdown
items.summary: More headaches are on the way as similar work on the 110-year-old Lake Street Bridge will require service disruptions this spring.

items.title: Nonbinary Chess Club Builds LGBTQ+ Connections Over Game Boards
items.summary: The club's next all-inclusive gatherings are Thursday at City Farm on Division Street and Sunday at Sweet Luxury Suites Downtown.

items.title: 31 Things To Do In Chicago This Weekend: Halloween Fun And More
items.summary: Parades, fall fests and Día de Los Muertos celebrations are on deck this weekend.

items.title: Project 50 seeks to export Illinois abortion‑rights playbook to red‑state races
items.summary: Illinois activists behind Project 50 are targeting local races in states with strict abortion bans, aiming to replicate the state’s pro‑choice success. The group has raised more than $3.7 million from 858 donors in 36 states, with Gov. JB Pritzker contributing $100,000 to its 2026 fundraising. Since its 2022 launch the organization has helped win seven legislative contests, including three victories in 2024 and four in 2025.

items.title: Seniors for Brandon Johnson endorse mayoral candidate amid new Senior Bill of Rights
items.summary: The affinity group Seniors for Brandon Johnson has officially endorsed incumbent Mayor Brandon Johnson, citing his recent executive order that created a Senior Bill of Rights. The order calls for safe housing, access to information, the right to organize, reporting problems and coordination of services for seniors across Chicago.

items.title: Chicago School Board oversees $10 billion budget, faces aging buildings and shrinking enrollment
items.summary: The Chicago Board of Education manages a $10 billion budget, larger than many major cities, while contending with aging school facilities, ballooning debt and declining student enrollment, according to a Tribune analysis.

items.title: Why restaurant surcharges linger
items.summary: Last week, Chicago writer Kit Graham ignited a firestorm by asking why local restaurants are still applying surcharges post-pandemic on top of just raising menu prices. Many Chicago diners have the same questions. What's happening: We queried the leaders at the city's largest restaurant groups to find out.

items.title: Mother Jones Monument Breaks Ground As Downtown’s First Honoring A Historic Woman
items.summary: The Mother Jones “We Shall Rise” Monument will honor the pioneering labor activist who got her start in Chicago.

items.title: Amtrak Protesters Vow To ‘Stop Ishbia In His Tracks’ As Developer Appears At Charity Conference
items.summary: Protesters rallied outside the Downtown Invest for Kids conference, opposing Amtrak’s proposed $915 million rail maintenance facility in Bridgeport and Chinatown.

items.title: Chicago REAL ID supercenter in the Loop to close at end of December
items.summary: Nearly two years after opening a downtown supercenter to process a surge in demand for REAL IDs, the Illinois Secretary of State's office plans to close the facility at the end of the year, saying it has fulfilled its mission.

items.title: 1 killed, 1 injured in shooting near a 7-Eleven in Chicago's Loop
items.summary: A man is dead and another injured after a shooting in The Loop early Wednesday morning.

items.summary: Officers responding to reports of a shooting around 2:40 a.m. Wednesday found two men with gunshot wounds outside on Lake Street, police said.

items.title: Some Green, Pink Line Stations To Remain Closed This Week Due To Lake Street Bridge Construction
items.summary: Full Pink and Green Line service is expected to be restored later this week, although an exact date and time has not been determined yet, officials said.

items.title: New COVID-19 Monument And Park Honors Chicago's Frontline Workers, Pandemic Victims
items.summary: IMD Park is the first new public park in the Illinois Medical District in decades. It features a soaring COVID-19 monument, fitness areas, a playground and more.

items.summary: Chicago police are investigating a deadly shooting in the Loop on Wednesday morning.

items.title: Cindy Bailey confronts Gov. JB Pritzker over campaign attacks ahead of Illinois governor race
items.summary: On Oct. 27, 2026, Cindy Bailey, wife of Republican gubernatorial candidate Darren Bailey, held a press conference at the Illinois State Capitol to criticize Gov. JB Pritzker’s ads that she says mischaracterize her husband’s views on women. She highlighted her 40‑year marriage, family farm, and her own floral shop as evidence of her husband’s respect for women, and warned that the attacks also disparage stay‑at‑home mothers. Bailey pivoted to the financial pressures facing families, citing child‑care, grocery, electricity, and car‑repair costs, and urged the governor to address those concerns directly.

items.title: State legislators introduce EDGE Essentials bill to expand tax credits for independent pharmacies and grocery stores
items.summary: State Rep. Will Guzzardi and State Sen. Doris Turner announced legislation called EDGE Essentials that would broaden the existing EDGE tax credit program to attract and grow independent pharmacies and grocery stores across Illinois. The proposal has backing from the Illinois Department of Commerce and Economic Opportunity and the Illinois Retail Merchants Association, aiming to support local businesses and improve community access to essential goods.

items.title: Evanston plans to close schools
items.summary: Evanston/Skokie District 65 needs to cut $20 million by 2028 and district leaders are pushing to do that by closing schools and cutting after-school care. Closing a school removes a community anchor and forces families to rebuild, and ending the childcare program disrupts working families. But district leaders argue that decades of unbalanced budgets have backed them into a corner.

items.title: Shooting investigation underway in The Loop
items.summary: A shooting investigation is underway in The Loop early Wednesday morning.

items.title: Work Finally Begins On DuSable Park, Nearly 40 Years After Land Was Set Aside For It
items.summary: Lakefront land was first set aside for the park in 1987. It is slated to be completed by summer 2028.

items.title: Street Vendors Rally For More Protections In Proposed Ordinance: Being A Worker Is Not A Crime'
items.summary: Restrictions on where and how long vendors can sell food and drink in Chicago continue to make it difficult to support their families, workers said.

items.title: Man dies after shooting involving FBI agent in Pilsen
items.summary: A man has died after a shooting involving an FBI agent on Chicago's Near West Side on Monday.

items.title: Ribbon cut for COVID-19 memorial in Illinois Medical District
items.summary: The ribbon was cut Tuesday for a COVID-19 memorial monument in the Illinois Medical District on Chicago's Near West Side.

items.title: The Oct. 28 Skyline is out
items.summary: The Oct. 28 edition of Skyline from Inside Publications is out. In his note to readers, editor Tom O'Gorman calls the midterm election a moment of real significance for Chicago and urges anyone who has not yet voted to cast a ballot by Election Day, Nov. 3.

items.title: Freight train looted on Chicago's Near West Side
items.summary: Thieves looted a freight train on Chicago’s West Side Tuesday morning, causing major delays for Metra commuters.

items.title: Shooting leaves 2 wounded in downtown Chicago 7-Eleven
items.summary: Police as of midday Tuesday were still searching for the shooter in the incident at the 7-Eleven at Adams Street and Wabash Avenue. Darius Johnson reports.

items.title: 2 wounded in shooting inside Loop 7-Eleven store, Chicago police say
items.summary: Two men were shot inside a 7-Eleven store in the Loop Monday night, Chicago police said.

items.title: Gov. JB Pritzker unveils Building Up Independent Local Developers (BUILD) Fund
items.summary: At a 10:30 a.m. press conference at City Hall on Oct 27, 2026, Governor JB Pritzker announced the BUILD Fund, a new financing program aimed at independent developers building projects in Chicago. The fund is intended to support local development in neighborhoods such as the West Loop, Fulton Market and the South Loop. Pritzker highlighted the fund’s role in creating jobs and expanding affordable housing.

items.title: Jean Baptiste Pointe DuSable Park groundbreaking ceremony held on Lake Shore Drive
items.summary: Governor JB Pritzker gave remarks at the groundbreaking for the Jean Baptiste Pointe DuSable Park on Lake Shore Drive at 12:30 p.m. on Oct 27, 2026. The ceremony marked the start of construction for a new waterfront park near the Loop that will feature public green space and river access. City officials said the park will enhance recreation options for residents of the Near West Side and South Loop.

items.title: Hospitality and labor groups urge City Council to reject liquor tax hike
items.summary: The Chicago Alcohol Tax Coalition, made up of hospitality, beverage and labor groups, is asking the City Council to reject a proposal in the $17.6 billion city budget to double the tax on beer, wine and spirits bought for off-site consumption, from 1.5% to 3%. The coalition says the increase would raise costs for consumers and squeeze neighborhood businesses.

items.title: Final day of petition filing draws more 2027 mayoral hopefuls
items.summary: Monday was the last day to turn in nominating signatures for the 2027 Chicago mayor's race. Filing on the final day were Comptroller Susana Mendoza, Cook County Treasurer Maria Pappas, Board of Review Commissioner George Cardenas, cardiologist Dr. Lisa Nee, attorney William Quinlan, entrepreneur Joe Holberg, Danielle Carter-Walters and Zoe Ma.

items.title: Big money flows into Chicago school board races
items.summary: Outside groups are spending heavily on Chicago's school board races ahead of the Nov. 3 election. The Our Schools PAC has spent more than $843,000, Chicago Teachers Union-related PACs have spent more than $1.6 million, and Common Ground Collective's independent expenditure arm has spent more than $5 million, according to the State Board of Elections.

items.title: Gov. JB Pritzker holds $46.4 million cash on hand as he seeks third term
items.summary: Illinois Governor JB Pritzker entered the week with $46.4 million in campaign cash while pursuing a third term. He recently donated $3,500 to Daniel Biss, the Democratic nominee for Congress in the 9th District, and is spending on signage that ties his Republican challenger Darren Bailey to former President Donald Trump. The governor also attended a groundbreaking at Jean Baptiste Pointe DuSable Park in the Loop, underscoring his continued presence in Chicago politics.

items.title: Chicago ballot questions
items.summary: Questions about a millionaire tax, a new gunshot detection system, a permanent fairgrounds space and compensation for Operation Midway Blitz damage round out Cook County residents' midterm ballots. While these are nonbinding questions, their answers can help legislators gauge public opinion and decide which laws to pursue. Gunshot detection "Should the City of Chicago restart the use of gunshot detection.

items.title: 2 men shot during fight inside 7-Eleven in The Loop
items.summary: Two men were shot during a fight inside a 7-Eleven in The Loop on Monday night.

items.title: 2 men shot inside 7-Eleven in The Loop
items.summary: Two men are in the hospital after a fight that led to a shooting at a 7-Eleven in The Loop on Monday night.

items.title: Public meetings planned for proposed Amtrak facility move from South Loop to Bridgeport
items.summary: According to a new public dashboard for the project, the Federal Railroad Administration is preparing an environmental assessment despite indications that it may be exempt. The FRA is also planning two public meetings, but no dates have been announced.

items.title: Lula comes from behind to win Brazil's presidential runoff
items.summary: Brazilian President Luiz Inacio Lula da Silva won the Oct. 25 runoff over Flavio Bolsonaro, the first come-from-behind second-round win in Brazil's democratic history. Turnout reached almost 81%, the highest for a runoff in 20 years, and the Brazilian real fell more than 10% against the dollar the next day. POLITICO Forecast also notes high turnout helped a student-led movement oust Serbia's Aleksandar Vucic the same day.

items.title: A Coworking Space That Never Closes: Switchyards 24/7 Work Clubs' Expand In Chicago
items.summary: The Atlanta-based company is opening locations in Lincoln Park and Fulton Market that aim to combine the look and feel of a cafe, hotel lobby and college library.

items.title: Drivers Have Blocked A Bike Lane By The Main Post Office For Years - Despite Free Parking Nearby
items.summary: Cyclists say cars, trucks and even postal police vehicles regularly block the Harrison Street lane, forcing riders to swerve into traffic. The city says it's planning to add protections to prevent this next month.

items.title: Mayor Brandon Johnson files 33,000 signatures as Chicago mayoral race kicks off
items.summary: On Friday, incumbent Mayor Brandon Johnson submitted roughly 33,000 signatures to the Chicago Board of Elections, meeting the 12,500‑signature threshold to appear on the ballot. The filing deadline for all mayoral candidates is today, with objections due by Nov. 2. Other declared candidates include Secretary of State Alexi Giannoulias, Congressman Mike Quigley, businessman Willie Wilson, lobbyist John Kelly and CHA Commissioner Matt Brewer.

items.title: Lincoln Legacy PAC launches six‑figure TV ad against former Rep. Melissa Bean in 8th District
items.summary: A Republican super PAC, Lincoln Legacy PAC, began airing a six‑figure television ad campaign across the Chicago area over the weekend targeting former congresswoman Melissa Bean, who is seeking to reclaim the 8th Congressional District seat. The ad accuses Bean of raising energy bills while opposing tax cuts.

items.title: Mayor Brandon Johnson files nominating petitions with 33,000 signatures as Chicago mayoral race heats up
items.summary: Mayor Brandon Johnson turned in roughly 33,000 signatures to the Chicago Board of Elections on Friday, meeting the 12,500‑signature requirement to appear on the ballot. The filing deadline for challengers is Nov. 2, and the field now includes Secretary of State Alexi Giannoulias, Congressman Mike Quigley, businessman Willie Wilson, lobbyist John Kelly, and CHA Commissioner Matt Brewer. Campaigns are expected to file objections and launch legal challenges in the coming days.

items.title: Gov. JB Pritzker receives United Auto Workers endorsement at South Side rally
items.summary: Governor JB Pritzker shook hands with United Auto Workers members after the union endorsed him on Oct. 25, 2026, during a rally on Chicago’s South Side. Pritzker highlighted the Big Three strike that began in 2023 and framed his campaign as a fight for better wages and benefits for workers. The endorsement comes as the governor and Republican challenger Darren Bailey intensify their outreach ahead of the Nov. 3 election.

items.title: Monday is the last day to file petitions in Chicago's 2027 mayoral race
items.summary: Oct. 26 is the final day for Chicago mayoral candidates to file nominating petitions with the Chicago Board of Elections. Candidates need 12,500 valid signatures, and the deadline to file objections to other candidates' petitions is Nov. 2. Mayor Brandon Johnson filed roughly 33,000 signatures on Friday, and Alexi Giannoulias, Mike Quigley, Willie Wilson, John Kelly and Matt Brewer are already in the race, with Comptroller Susana Mendoza expected to file today.

items.title: Kennedy Expressway commutes remain slow three years after the rehab began
items.summary: A WBEZ analysis found most of the longest Kennedy Expressway commutes on record happened during the three-year rehab project, as the state spent more than $170 million on the 7.5-mile stretch between Downtown and the Edens junction. The Sun-Times also reported that delays during the work were the worst in more than 20 years.

items.title: What's up with Bally's graffiti?
items.summary: Graffiti on the exterior of Bally's Chicago hotel tower has sat untouched for at least two months, becoming emblematic of the casino project's construction delays. Bally's has faced a series of setbacks in its River West casino, hotel and entertainment project. Its August announcement that it was pausing work added another wrinkle in the long-awaited project that promises to pour about $200 million into city.

items.title: Graffiti on Bally's River West tower highlights casino construction delays
items.summary: Graffiti on the exterior of the Bally's Chicago hotel tower near Grand Avenue has gone untouched for at least two months. Bally's paused work on nongaming amenities in August amid a dispute with the city over the 2026 budget's legalization of video gambling terminals, and says crews are now focused on the casino floor. The project is expected to send about $200 million a year to city pension funds.

items.title: Judges fill most of the Chicago midterm ballot: how retention votes work
items.summary: Most questions on Chicago's Nov. 3 ballot involve judges, with more than 60 Cook County judges up for retention. Retained judges need 60% approval, and only three have failed to win retention in the last six years. Voter guides with recommendations are available from the Chicago Bar Association and the Illinois Alliance of Bar Associations.

items.title: Midinight book release parties planned in Chicago for latest in "A Court of Thorns and Roses" series
items.summary: Fans of the "A Court of Thorns and Roses" book series were set Monday night to flock to a Target store in the West Loop.

items.title: Midnight release parties set for latest in ACOTAR series
items.summary: Fans of the “A Court of Thorns and Roses” book series were set Monday night to flock to a Target store in the West Loop.

items.title: Feds Finally Agree To Environmental Review Of Proposed Amtrak Facility In Bridgeport
items.summary: The Federal Railroad Administration’s decision follows months of opposition to the proposed maintenance facility near Rate Field, where residents have raised concerns about its potential environmental and health effects.

items.title: Midterm campaign enters its final week as Republicans brace for House losses
items.summary: POLITICO Forecast reports that polls suggest Republicans are likely to lose the U.S. House and face a struggle to hold the Senate as the Nov. 3 midterms approach, with gas prices tied to the Iran war a top voter concern. President Trump holds a rally in Mississippi on Monday, a state where Democrats see a rare Senate opening.

items.title: CTA service interruptions on Pink and Green Lines continue through Oct 28
items.summary: Structural, electrical and mechanical work on the new leaf of the Lake Street Bridge forces Pink and Green Line service interruptions between Clinton and Clark/Lake stations until 4 a.m. on Oct 28, with free bus substitutions operating on that segment. Green Line trains run in two sections, connecting at Clinton and Clark/Lake stations, while Pink Line riders must transfer to the Blue Line at Racine Station or use 9/X9 Ashland buses for downtown service. The CTA advises riders to check its website for additional information.

items.title: CTA Pink and Green Line service interruptions continue through Oct 28 due to Lake Street Bridge work
items.summary: The CTA announced that because of additional work on the new leaf of the Lake Street Bridge, Pink and Green Line service between the Clinton and Clark/Lake stations will be suspended until 4 a.m. on October 28. Free bus substitutions will run between those stations, and Green Line trains will operate in two sections with all‑stop service on each side of the disruption. Pink Line riders can transfer at Racine to the Blue Line or use the 9/X9 Ashland buses for connections to the West Loop and downtown.

items.title: Pink and Green Line closure at Lake Street Bridge extended to Oct. 28
items.summary: Pink and Green Line service between Clinton and Clark/Lake stations will stay interrupted until 4 a.m. on Wednesday, Oct. 28, to finish structural, electrical and mechanical work on the new Lake Street Bridge leaf. Free shuttle buses continue between Clinton and Clark/Lake, and Green Line trains run in two sections. Pink Line riders should transfer to the Blue Line at Racine, or take the 9/X9 Ashland bus to reach Ashland, Morgan, Clinton and the West Loop.

items.title: Pizzeria Gabbo Opens in Fulton Market
items.summary: The West Central Association highlights the opening of Pizzeria Gabbo in Fulton Market, offering pizza, pasta, and gelato. The new restaurant is a member of the WCA and adds to the neighborhood’s growing culinary scene.

items.title: O’Hare Flyer Project Discussed at WCA Speaker Series
items.summary: The WCA Speaker Series on November 17 will feature a conversation with the team behind the O’Hare Flyer, a proposed transportation project connecting Chicago and O’Hare International Airport. The session will include a presentation and Q&A and is scheduled for noon–2 p.m. at The Green at 320.

items.title: 1133 W. Kinzie development moves forward with new Pizzeria Gabbo
items.summary: The West Loop development at 1133 W. Kinzie is progressing, adding a new pizza, pasta and gelato venue called Pizzeria Gabbo in Fulton Market. The project expands dining options in the neighborhood and reflects ongoing commercial growth in the area.

items.title: Pizza Lobo networking event for West Loop professionals
items.summary: The West Loop’s newly opened Pizza Lobo will host a networking gathering on Wednesday, November 11 from 4 p.m. to 6 p.m. at 165 N. Morgan Street. Attendees can enjoy pizza, drinks and conversation while connecting with local business owners and professionals.

items.title: Free WCA member workshop Oct. 27: build a 90-day plan for your business
items.summary: The West Central Association is hosting a free, hands-on working session for member business owners on Tuesday, Oct. 27, led by Dan Brown, The Growth Coach of West Loop/Chicagoland. Participants will look at revenue per hour, where revenue comes from and how their time is spent, then leave with a written 90-day plan. Seating is limited and RSVP is required.

items.title: Homerathon brings a full read-aloud of The Odyssey to Greektown Oct. 29-30
items.summary: The National Hellenic Museum in Greektown and UIC's Department of Classics and Mediterranean Studies are reading Homer's Odyssey aloud from beginning to end on Thursday, Oct. 29 (12:30-8 p.m.) and Friday, Oct. 30 (10 a.m.-4 p.m.). A Thursday happy hour from 6-8 p.m. invites visitors to grab a drink and read a passage. The museum's exhibit The Odyssey Reimagined is also on view Thursdays through Sundays.

items.title: Green, Pink Line Service Disruptions Extended Due Lake Street Bridge Work
items.summary: Green and Pink line service to the Loop was scheduled to resume Monday, but that date was pushed back to Wednesday due to ongoing bridge replacement work.

items.title: CTA Green, Pink Line trains to be disrupted for extra 2 days
items.summary: For two more days longer than originally planned, the CTA Green and Pink lines will not be connecting to the Loop from the West Side.

items.title: Arts in the Dark Parade draws nearly 100,000 spectators downtown Chicago
items.summary: Downtown Chicago came alive for the 12th annual Arts in the Dark Parade, featuring floats, dancers, and music celebrating the arts.

items.title: Arts in the Dark Parade brings creativity to life in downtown Chicago
items.summary: Chicago’s kickoff to Halloween festivities paraded down Columbus Drive in Grant Park Saturday night, as the 12th annual Arts in the Dark Parade brought together more than 100 cultural organizations. Jackie Kostek reports.

items.title: Another suspicious letter delivered to government building downtown Chicago, officials say
items.summary: Chicago firefighters responded yet again after a suspicious letter was sent to a federal building in the city.
